reasoning: French loan, no glottal stop in it, so I respell تركوأز as تُرْكْوَاز with a long aa. Used as an invariable colour word.
Hollow verb with long aa and ق as a glottal stop: saa', imperfect bisuu'. The everyday Ramallah verb for driving a car.
The article assimilates to the sun letter ش with a shadda: ish-shimaal. In running speech 3ala contracts to 3a, giving 3ash-shimaal.
Accurate as MSA Form IV, initial hamza written as the bare vowel. A Ramallah speaker uses the Form II verb instead, ballagh, as in ballagh ish-shurTa.
haad is the Palestinian 'this'. ذ is said as plain z in this verb, so I respell it بِزَكِّرْنِي, a b-imperfect with the object -ni; the frame ends in the preposition bi-.
The hamza is pronounced and written ', and the taa marbuta after it is a: madfa'a. Understood and used in Ramallah, though for a gas or kerosene heater people usually say soobya.
ع is 3 and emphatic ض is D: 3ariiD. Of a road, a shoulder or a stripe; for a wide space Palestinians say waasi3.
3am plus the b-imperfect is the Palestinian progressive. The verb shatta 'to rain' is feminine here with id-dinya understood as the subject.
ذ is said as plain z in this word, so أستاذ is respelled أُسْتَاز; the initial hamza is written as the bare vowel. Used as a title of address as well as for a teacher.
English loan in two parts, the second with ee rather than ii: tii sheert. Written as two words, as in the entry.
bi- plus the article assimilates to the sun letter ن: bin-nisbe, taa marbuta as e after ب. The frame ends in the preposition la-, which attaches to whatever follows.
Emphatic ص as S with a final cluster: maSr, with a fatha rather than the MSA kasra of miSr.
ح is 7, and the Palestinian masculine form is 7ilu, i then u. It stretches from 'sweet' to 'pretty', 'nice' and 'good' of almost anything.
mumkin plus a bare imperfect is the Palestinian polite request. The Palestinian prefix is ti-, and ع is 3: ti3iid, to a man.
CiCiC past kibir 'grew'. mukhkh 'brain' doubles its خ before the suffix -o, written khkh as in mit'akhkher. Idiomatic for someone who has grown up and started thinking straight.
Two short i vowels: simsim. The sesame seed itself; the paste is Ta7iine.
ع is 3, short i, taa marbuta as e after ب: 3ilbe. Covers a cardboard box, a tin and a packet alike.
Both ق are glottal stops and the stative past is CiCiC: 'ili'. Most often heard in the negative imperative, ma ti'la', 'don't worry'; the participle 'al'aan is also common.
bi- plus the article, with the hamza written after the prefix as in il-'usbuu3, and emphatic ض as D. Usually continued as bil-'iDaafe la-heek.
Form VIII participle with Palestinian i vowels: mistiwi. Said of food cooked through and of fruit that has ripened.

meaning_fix: sufficiently / adequately; as a bare 'enough' a Ramallah speaker says kfaaye or bikaffi
reasoning: As written this is bi- plus kifaaye, an adverbial 'in sufficient measure', taa marbuta as e after ي. Standing alone for 'enough' it sounds Egyptian; in Ramallah you hear kfaaye or the verb bikaffi.
mudiir has long ii; م is a moon letter so the article stays il-, and the taa marbuta is e after س.
ح is 7 and the final ث is written th. This is an academic word, and many Ramallah speakers say it with s, ba7s, since urban ث shifts to s in learned vocabulary.
Doubled verb, the shadda doubling ب: kabb, imperfect bikibb. Used for pouring out, spilling and chucking something in the bin.
beet has ee, not ii, and ب is a moon letter so the article stays il-. ktiir is the Palestinian 'very', with the first short vowel dropped.
